newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sentences 39 Serbs to prison.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sentences 39 Serbs to prison.

text.p: A county court in the Adriatic port of Split on Monday sentenced 39 Serbs accused of war crimes to prison terms of five to 20 years, state news agency HINA said.

The men, 27 of whom were tried in absentia, were charged with taking part in ethnic cleansing of Croatians, including murder and torture of civilians and prisoners of war near Sinj in the hinterland of Split, Hina said.

"All 39 men were accused of war crimes, and not for taking part in the armed rebellion," the agency added, without specifying if they were Croatian citizens or members of the Yugoslav army which backed Serb rebels in 1991.

Croatia issued a general amnesty law for all the Serbs who took part in the 1991 rebellion against the Croatian bid for independence from federal Yugoslavia, with the exception of suspected war criminals.
Thirteen of the 39 Serbs were sentenced to a maximum prison term of 20 years, while two of them were also permanently banned from entering Croatia.
